title: Stock redemption planning — Marsh Corp.
instructions: Marsh Corp. has 100 shares of one class outstanding and accumulated E&P of $500,000. Ivy owns 50 shares (basis $20,000 in total) and her son owns 30 shares. An unrelated investor owns the other 20. Marsh redeems 20 of Ivy's shares for $100,000. Compute the amounts and answer the questions.

exhibits.title: Rules
exhibits.content:
- §318 family attribution: an individual is treated as owning shares owned by her children.
- §302(b)(2): after the redemption, the shareholder must own less than 50% of the voting stock and less than 80% of her percentage before the redemption.

rows.label: Ivy's ownership before the redemption, with attribution
Ivy's ownership after the redemption, with attribution
Dividend income to Ivy
rows.explanation: The redemption fails §302(b)(2) (75% is not below 64% or 50%) and isn't a complete termination, so the full 100,000 is a dividend (E&P is ample).

rows.label: Ivy's basis in her remaining 30 shares
rows.explanation: The 8,000 basis of the redeemed shares shifts to her remaining shares: **20,000**.

rows.label: Ivy's gain if the son were unrelated (no attribution)
rows.explanation: Without attribution: 30 ÷ 80 = 37.5%, below 40% (80% of 50%) and 50%, so it is an exchange: 100,000 − 8,000 = **92,000** capital gain.

rows.label: Treatment of the redemption with attribution
rows.explanation: A redemption that fails all §302(b) tests is a §301 distribution — here a dividend.

rows.label: Which change would most likely give Ivy exchange treatment?
options: Redeem all of Ivy's shares and have her waive family attribution
Redeem 5 more of the son's shares instead
Pay Ivy in property instead of cash
rows.answer: Redeem all of Ivy's shares and have her waive family attribution
rows.explanation: A complete termination with a family attribution waiver under §302(c)(2) qualifies for exchange treatment.

rows.label: Does Marsh recognize gain on redeeming shares for cash?
rows.explanation: A corporation recognizes no gain distributing cash; gain arises only on distributing appreciated property (§311(b)).
